text:
carla: Heads-up — we're kicking off a sandbox -> airgapped (on-prem) migration test for a single tenant tomorrow. wanted to surface a few security questions before we run the drill.
ben: Nice. what areas are you most worried about?
carla: RBAC changes (service accounts + human admin access), KMS key handoff/rotation, and ensuring audit logs are captured off-cluster without outbound internet. also netpols to minimize blast radius.
priya: For RBAC, we should stage a scoped role binding that mirrors the eventual prod binding. test rollback path too. small and reversible.
dan: Agree. Also add a canary workload that intentionally fails access — exercise least-privilege checks.
carla: @dan good call. we need a checklist. I'll propose items, please poke holes: 1) create migration-rbac namespace w/ restricted roles, 2) provision tenant KMS key in HSM proxy, 3) deploy audit-forwarder to internal log collector (no egress), 4) apply networkpolicy deny-by-default + explicit egress to KMS proxy and NTP, 5) run vuln scan + simulated incident.
kate: For (2) — how are we proxying KMS? we discussed a small MTLS proxy that runs in the VPC and talks to customer HSM over private link. important to pin certs and enforce mTLS client auth.
paul: The proxy also handles key rotation requests. we need a clarified API: rotate, rewrap, get-key-metadata. prefer a thin shim to avoid secrets in pods.
infra: On egress, recommend using a dedicated egress gateway that enforces SNI and destination IP allowlist. netpols should only allow pod -> egress-gw:443. egress-gw then does NAT to internal services.
priya: Sample k8s netpol for restricted egress (very conservative):
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-all-egress-except-kms
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: migration-canary
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          role: kms-proxy
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```
carla: Perfect. we should also lock down DNS — only allow the cluster DNS resolver + internal resolver.
ben: Audit logs — we can't forward to external SaaS. plan: forward to a collector in the VPC (fluent-bit -> s3-compatible on-prem object store) and mirror a copy to an immutable store for retention. make sure logs are signed.
paul: Signing logs is key for tamper evidence. we can use a signing key in the HSM and push a detached signature per batch.
dan: Vulnerability triage: run the scanner in offline mode, record artifact hashes, and keep CVE allowance list for the drill. also practice a CVE escalation path.
carla: Incident drill scenario: compromised service account obtains pod token and tries to call model-serving endpoint and KMS rotate. detection signals: 1) unusual service account token usage, 2) anomalous egress to KMS proxy endpoints, 3) high rate of key-rotation API calls.
kate: Add more: 4) unexpected audit log deletion or gaps, 5) new clusterrolebindings created.
secops-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT-DRILL-REG: Please file a post-drill ticket in #incidents with logs attached and mark severity code DRILL.
priya: Runbook steps for the drill (short):
- step 0: notify infra + secops and create ephemeral channel
- step 1: isolate the canary namespace (kubectl label)
- step 2: block egress from canary via egress-gw blackhole rule
- step 3: rotate KMS keys (HSM) and revoke service account tokens
- step 4: collect all audit logs and signatures, verify immutability
- step 5: restore from last-known-good snapshot and validate workloads
carla: Questions: 1) who can perform step 3 in airgapped prod? 2) how do we safely revoke tokens without breaking other tenants?
ben: Step 3 should be secops + platform lead only. we need a scoped revoke that targets only the compromised service account via kubectl auth revoke or tokencontroller rotation. avoid cluster-wide crash.
paul: We should implement a label-based token revocation helper: tokens with label "migration-canary=true" can be revoked in one command. also ensure OIDC-issued tokens can be short-lived.
dan: On key rotation safety: do a rewrap + double-write pattern: new key created, wrapped copies stored, traffic fallback to old key for 5m, then cutover. document steps in the playbook.
carla: Action items: @ben to draft RBAC restricted role + rollback cmd, @kate to detail KMS-proxy TLS cert pinning + API surface, @infra to add egress-gw rules and netpol template, @paul to draft log signing integration, @priya to author the drill runbook. due EOD tomorrow so we can rehearse Friday.
ben: i'll take RBAC. quick Q: prefer k8s rolebinding patch or create new ClusterRole? i think Role in namespace is safer.
kate: KMS proxy TLS: use certs minted by our internal CA, set TLS min version = 1.3, and validate SAN includes proxy DNS + IP. will write a checklist.
infra: i'll spin up the egress-gw changes in staging and post the commands here.
paul: i'll prototype the signing lambda-equivalent that runs in airgapped infra and outputs detached .sig per log file.
secops-bot: :thumbsup: Drill scheduled. keep me posted in the channel.
carla: thanks all — if anyone sees a missing risk call it out now. otherwise i'll create the migration-drill channel and link tasks. :lock:
